stories: You are the class leader in Class 11, and your teacher steps out for a meeting. She says, "Write down the names of anyone who talks." The room slowly turns noisy, and when she returns, she asks for the list. Your best friend, who sat beside you through every exam and shared her lunchbox when you forgot yours, is on it. Your pen stops moving. Your eyes sting, and you cannot tell whether you are more afraid of the teacher or of losing your friend's trust.

You are the captain of your college cricket team, and the coach asks you to help finalise the squad for the inter-university tournament. Your close friend on the team, who has stood by you since the first week of hostel life, has worked harder than anyone, but he has not improved enough. That night you sit with the list on your phone, unable to type his name. You remember your grandfather saying, "Boys don't cry," so you hold it in, and the lump in your throat only grows.

At twenty-four, you have just been made a team lead. Your manager asks for honest ratings, and you know a low rating for a colleague will affect her bonus. She helped you through your first confusing month, and this year has been hard for her at home. You go to the washroom and cry quietly, worried that if anyone sees you, they will say you are "too emotional" to lead.
helps: Let the feeling be real. Tears that come from caring are nothing to be ashamed of.
Say it to someone you trust. A parent, an elder, a coach, a close friend or a cousin can help you put it plainly: "I care about this person, and I have to do something hard."
Ask one question: "What is the honest and kind thing to do?"
Be firm without being cruel, because the person in front of you carries the same Self as you.
Try this today: Tell one trusted person about something that is weighing on your heart.
2.1.read: tam tathaa kripayaa-vishtam ashru-poorna-aakulekshanam | visheedantam idam vaakyam uvaacha madhusoodanah
2.1.meaning: Arjuna was filled with pity and sorrow, his eyes full of tears and his mind troubled. Then Krishna spoke to him.
2.1.bhakti: Krishna does not call Arjuna's tears wrong. He stays beside him. When love and duty pull in two directions, we can offer both to Him in prayer. The same God sits in the heart of the person we have to disappoint.

stories: It is the night before your Class 12 chemistry practical, and you have done every experiment in the lab many times. Lying in bed, your mind fills with "What if I spill it? What if I forget the steps?" By morning you tell your mother, "I don't want to go." She does not scold you. She sits beside you and asks softly, "Where is this coming from? You have done this very experiment ten times." Her question gives you a small gap in which to breathe.

You have cleared the written test and the group discussion, and now it is the final round of campus placement. In the waiting hall, your hands are cold, and you whisper to a friend, "Maybe I should leave. They will find me out." A senior walks over and says, "Is that really you talking, or just the fear? Let's go through your project once, slowly." By the time your name is called, the fog has thinned.

It is your first big client presentation at work. Ten minutes before, a familiar thought returns: "Everyone here is smarter than me, and today they will realise it." You ask your team lead if someone else could present. She says calmly, "We chose you because of your work. Is this a fact, or just a feeling?" You take a sip of water, open your slides and realise you know them well.
helps: Pause and ask: "Is this a fact, or a fog?"
Take three slow breaths.
Remember one real proof of your effort, such as the practice you did, the project you finished or the slides you made.
Tell someone who knows you, like a parent, a sibling or a close friend. They can often see your steadiness when you cannot.
Try this today: Before something big, say a short prayer: "Lord, be with me. I will do my part."
2.2.read: kutas tvaa kashmalam idam vishame samupasthitam | anaarya-jushtam asvargyam akeerti-karam arjuna
2.2.meaning: Krishna said, "Arjuna, how has this fog of confusion come over you at such a serious moment? Good people do not hold on to it. It will not lift you up, and it will not bring you a good name."
2.2.bhakti: Krishna's first words are a question, not a scolding, because He knows Arjuna's true nature is stronger than the fog. A short prayer before a big moment can bring that steadiness back.

stories: Your Class 12 results come, and the marks are lower than you had hoped. Your friends celebrate the colleges they got into, and you shut your door and tell your family, "I will just sit out this year." After a while, your older cousin knocks, sits beside you and says gently, "Wash your face. Then let's look at all the options you really have." It is hard to move, but you get up and splash water on your face, and for the first time that day you take a deep breath.

You have a backlog in one subject, and you feel that everyone is thinking, "What will people say?" You stop going to class and tell your roommate, "What is the point?" She does not argue. She says, "Come, let's have tea at the canteen, and then we will plan the supplementary exam." Walking to the canteen is the first step back.

In your second month at work, a bug appears in your first project, and your manager mentions it in front of the whole team. That evening on the metro, you think of quitting. A senior who noticed your face messages you, "It happens to everyone. Let's fix it together tomorrow morning." You send a thumbs-up, and for the first time that day, the world feels less final.
helps: Do one small act of standing up. Wash your face, drink water, step outside or message one person.
Make a simple plan for the next small step, with a cousin, a friend or an elder who has been through something similar.
Remember: feelings of failure are heavy, but they are not the whole of you.
Try this today: Write down one small thing you will do tomorrow morning.
2.3.read: klaibyam maa sma gamah paartha naitat tvayy upapadyate | kshudram hridaya-daurbalyam tyaktvottishtha parantapa
2.3.meaning: "Do not give in to this loss of spirit, Arjuna. It does not suit you. Shake off this small weakness of the heart and stand up."
2.3.bhakti: Krishna says "stand up" with great affection, and He believes in Arjuna before Arjuna believes in himself. The word translated as "unmanliness" really means loss of spirit, which can happen to anyone, and anyone can recover it with His grace.

stories: You are in Class 12 and have reached the final of the inter-school science quiz. The other finalist is a senior from your own school who gave up his lunch breaks last year to coach you for free. When the quizmaster reads the first question, you know the answer, but your hand hesitates above the buzzer. It feels strange to compete against the person who taught you how.

A senior who helped you rewrite your resume and practise mock interviews has reached the last round of the same company's hiring, along with you. There are only two seats. One small voice inside you feels jealous of her, and another voice feels guilty for feeling that way. You wonder if trying your best against her is a kind of betrayal.

At work, your mentor shares his plan in a team review. He taught you how to write clear reports, and you owe him a lot. But you spot a mistake that could affect the whole project. You feel torn: correcting him in front of everyone seems disrespectful, but staying silent could harm the team.
helps: Say thank you first. Before the moment, silently thank the person who taught you.
Do your honest best. Respect does not mean holding back or staying silent.
Speak kindly and politely. In the last case, you might say privately, "May I check one thing in the plan with you?"
Notice jealousy without feeding it. It is a normal feeling. Remember that the same Self lives in them and in you, and try to be glad for what they have achieved.
Try this today: Send a thank-you message to a teacher or an elder who helped you.
2.4.read: katham bheeshmam aham sankhye dronam cha madhusoodana | ishubhih pratiyotsyaami poojaarhaav arisoodana
2.4.meaning: "Krishna, how can I fight Bhishma and Drona with my arrows in battle? They deserve my deepest respect."
2.4.gem: Same Self in all (respect, gratitude and healthy competition)
2.4.bhakti: The Gita never calls Arjuna's respect for his elders wrong. A grateful heart is part of devotion, and a good teacher carries a light that comes from God.

stories: In Class 10, your group project has been guided by your teacher for many weeks. Then a friend's older brother offers you a ready-made model and says, "Submit this as yours, and you will win the prize." You would get higher marks than your own work could earn. But you remember the evenings your teacher stayed back to help, and the prize starts to feel empty before you even win it.

In your final year, your team's app was mostly built by a senior who stayed up many nights helping you. A teammate suggests, "Let's present it as our own work. The judges will never know, and we will win the competition." You realise that a medal won this way would make every celebration feel hollow.

At work, your manager offers to put your name first on a project that a quiet colleague did most of the work on. It would look good for your next promotion. That evening, you cannot enjoy your tea. You keep thinking, "Could I look her in the eye tomorrow?"
helps: Ask yourself: "Will I be able to enjoy this and look myself in the mirror tomorrow?"
Choose the smaller success that is honestly yours.
Share credit freely. Say out loud who helped you, and name them in front of others.
Be big-hearted. A generous person gives the credit away and still feels rich.
Try this today: Thank, by name, someone who helped you recently.
2.5.read: guroon ahatvaa hi mahaanubhaavaan shreyo bhoktum bhaikshyam apeeha loke | hatvaartha-kaamaams tu guroon ihaiva bhunjeeya bhogaan rudhira-pradigdhaan
2.5.meaning: "It is better to live on simple food than to harm my noble teachers. If I harmed them, every pleasure I gained would be stained with the pain I caused."
2.5.gem: Mindful action (honesty, gratitude and sharing credit)
2.5.bhakti: Arjuna chooses gratitude over gain. A heart that stays thankful to its teachers is already close to God, because He lives in them too.

stories: You are in Class 10, and everyone is asking whether you will choose science, commerce or arts. Your friends have already decided, and you honestly do not know what you are good at. Your parents have suggested a direction based on what they see in you, and your teachers have their own views. You feel behind, as if everyone else was handed a map. You sit down with your parents and a teacher you trust, and together you look at your interests and strengths one at a time.

In your final year of college, you have a stable job offer, and a friend invites you to join a small startup. Elders tell you to take the safe offer. Your friends say to take the risk. You make a list on paper again and again, but each time you end up exactly where you started, unable to tell which is better.

After a year at your first job, you receive two offers. One is in your home city, near your family, with a smaller role. The other is in a bigger city with a better role, but far from home. Both have good points, and neither is guaranteed to turn out well.
helps: Say it calmly: "I do not know yet, and that is okay."
List what you truly value, and talk to two or three trusted people, such as your parents, an elder in the family or a teacher.
Choose the next step, not your whole life.
Give it your best, and stay open to changing course.
Try this today: Write down three things you enjoy doing and three things people say you are good at.
2.6.read: na chaitad vidmah kataran no gareeyo yad vaa jayema yadi vaa no jayeyuh | yaan eva hatvaa na jijeevishaamas te 'vasthitaah pramukhe dhaartaraashtraah
2.6.meaning: "I do not even know which is better for us: to fight or not to fight, to win or to lose. The very people we would not want to live without are standing in front of us."
2.6.bhakti: Arjuna openly says, "I do not know." That honesty is where he begins to learn. We too can offer our confusion to God and ask, "Show me the next step."

stories: You are in Class 11, and exams are close. You have watched videos, read posts and listened to friends, and each one says something different: study for twelve hours, study smart, sleep early, give up your phone. You feel more confused every day. One evening you close everything and go to your favourite teacher. "I do not know how to prepare," you say. "Please guide me." She sits with you and makes a simple weekly plan, and you feel your shoulders drop.

You are in your third year of college, and your feed is full of job posts, certificates and advice from seniors who all say different things. You have always believed that asking for help is a sign of weakness, so you have kept quiet. Finally you walk into the placement mentor's room and say, "I am not sure where to begin." The mentor smiles and says, "Good. Now we can actually start."

In your first month at work, you do not understand a process, but you nod in meetings so you do not look foolish. A week later, a small mistake appears because of it. You go to a senior and say, "I have not understood this. Can you walk me through it?" She says, "I wish I had asked that when I started."
helps: Choose one or two guides, such as a parent, a grandparent, a teacher or a senior, instead of listening to everyone.
Say it plainly: "I do not know. Please guide me."
Listen fully. Elders often carry lessons they learned the hard way, so hear them out before you decide.
Try what they suggest, and go back to tell them how it went.
Try this today: Write three questions for a person you respect, and ask one of them.
2.7.read: kaarpanya-doshopahata-svabhaavah prichchhaami tvaam dharma- sammoodha-chetaah | yach chhreyah syaan nishchitam broohi tan me shishyas te 'ham shaadhi maam tvaam prapannam
2.7.meaning: "My heart is heavy with helplessness, and my mind is confused about what is right. Please tell me clearly what is truly good for me. I am your student, and I have come to you for shelter. Please teach me."
2.7.gem: Mindful action (learning with an open heart, and respect for elders and teachers)
2.7.bhakti: Arjuna says, "I am your student, teach me." Asking for guidance with an open heart is itself a prayer, and the wisest teacher we meet carries a light from God.

stories: You score top marks in Class 10, and everyone congratulates you. Your family is proud, and your phone is full of messages. That night, you lie awake feeling strangely empty. You think, "I have everything I wanted, so why do I feel like this?" You say nothing, because everyone has told you that you should be happy.

You get the placement you dreamed of and post the news. A week later, you feel flat. You scroll for hours without enjoying anything, and you notice yourself comparing your offer with a friend's bigger one. You tell yourself you have no right to complain, since so many friends are still searching.

After two years of hard work, you finally get the promotion. The team celebrates, and your family is delighted. On Sunday evening, the same quiet heaviness returns, and you notice your mind already chasing the next level.
helps: Say it out loud to a parent, a sibling, a friend or an elder you trust: "I got what I wanted, and I still feel empty."
Let thankfulness and emptiness sit together. Both can be true.
Count what you already have. A gratitude list slowly changes what you notice.
Feed the inside. Spend time on a walk, a prayer, music, or helping someone.
Try this today: Write three things you are grateful for, and tell one person about them.
2.8.note: If the heaviness stays for many days, talk to a family member you trust, such as a parent, a grandparent or an elder.
2.8.read: na hi prapashyaami mamaapanudyaad yach chhokam uchchhoshanam indriyaanaam | avaapya bhoomaav asapatnam riddham raajyam suraanaam api chaadhipatyam
2.8.meaning: "I cannot see anything that will take away this sorrow that is drying up my strength, even if I won a rich kingdom on earth with no rivals, or even became ruler over the gods."
2.8.gem: Evenness (what truly fills the heart: gratitude and contentment)
2.8.bhakti: Even a great warrior like Arjuna learned that no kingdom can fill the heart. The lasting fullness comes from within, from the Self and from God.

stories: After a week of tests, an argument with a close friend and a scolding at home, you say to yourself, "I am done with everything." You stop answering messages and lie quietly in the dark. You have not decided anything. You just have no words left.

You live in a hostel, far from home, and your roommates are out most evenings. You start to feel unnoticed, so you skip a few classes and keep your phone on silent. Your mother calls three times, and you let it ring because you do not know how to explain.
After a month of late nights and a harsh review, you mute every work chat and sit on the balcony, unable to reply to anyone. It feels as if nothing you do makes a difference.
helps: Go easy on yourself.
Do one tiny thing: drink water, eat something, step outside.
Send one line to a friend, a sibling or a parent: "I am not okay right now."
If the silence lasts for days, tell a parent, a grandparent or an elder you trust.
Try this today: Send that one line to one person.
2.9.read: evam uktvaa hrisheekesham gudaakeshah parantapa | na yotsya iti govindam uktvaa tooshneem babhoova ha
2.9.meaning: After saying this to Krishna, Arjuna said, "I will not fight," and became silent.
2.9.gem: My steady Self (silence is not the end)
2.9.bhakti: Arjuna's silence is not the end of the story, because Krishna waits right beside him. When you have no words left, a silent prayer is enough.

stories: You come home upset about an exam paper and sit quietly in your room. Your grandmother does not ask a hundred questions or give a lecture. She sits beside you, hands you a glass of warm milk and says, "Drink this first. Then we will talk." Her calm makes the problem feel a little smaller.

It has been a hard day in the hostel, and you feel low. Your elder cousin, who went through the same course a few years ago, comes on a video call. He does not tell you what to do. He says, "Tell me everything, I am listening." By the end of the call, you are laughing at something small.

At work, a new joiner in your team looks shaken after a harsh review. You do not rush in with advice. You sit beside them, offer a cup of tea and say, "Whenever you want to talk, I am here." Your calm gives them room to breathe.
helps: Let a calm person in, such as a grandparent, an elder you trust or a close friend.
When someone else is struggling, sit beside them and listen first. Sharing your time and calm is a gift.
Take three slow breaths before you speak to anyone who is upset.
Try this today: Offer to sit with someone who looks like they are having a hard day.
2.10.read: tam uvaacha hrisheekeshah prahasann iva bhaarata | senayor ubhayor madhye visheedantam idam vachah
2.10.meaning: Then, in the middle of the two armies, Krishna spoke these words to the sorrowful Arjuna, with a gentle smile.
2.10.bhakti: Krishna stays steady in the middle of Arjuna's storm. The same God lives in the heart of the person who is hurting, so when we sit calmly with them, we are keeping Him company too.

stories: You are the friend everyone calls for advice. You tell a classmate, "Marks don't define you," and you mean it. Then your own results come in lower than you expected, and you spiral for days, forgetting every word you said. Your elder sibling notices and asks, "What would you tell your friend if she were in your place?"

You comforted a friend after a painful breakup and said, "You are worth more than this, and time will help." A few months later, your own relationship ends, and you cannot hear those words at all. A cousin who knew about the earlier conversation gently reminds you, "You said the same thing to your friend, remember?"

At work, you tell a junior colleague, "Mistakes are how we learn." Then you make a big mistake yourself and beat yourself up for a week. A friend from your first team says quietly, "Would you speak to your junior the way you are speaking to yourself?"
helps: Hear your own advice as if a friend were saying it to you.
Write down the kind words you give to others, and read them on a hard day.
Ask an elder sibling, a cousin or a close friend to remind you of them when you forget.
Try this today: Write one piece of advice you once gave someone, and read it to yourself.
2.11.read: ashochyaan anvashochas tvam prajnaa-vaadaamsh cha bhaashase | gataasoon agataasoomsh cha naanushochanti panditaah
2.11.meaning: Krishna said, "You are sad about things that do not need such sorrow, yet you speak words of wisdom. Wise people do not grieve over those who have gone or those who are still here."
2.11.gem: My steady Self (the wisdom is already in you)
2.11.bhakti: Krishna begins with honesty and affection. He sees the wise person in Arjuna before Arjuna does. The wisdom you give to others comes from the same Self within you.

stories: In Class 10, the group of friends you shared your lunch with starts leaving you out. It feels as if you have disappeared. At home, one of your parents sits with you and says gently, "You were you before this group, and you will still be you after it."

You trained for months for a place on the college team, and you did not get selected. For a long time you thought of yourself as "the sports person," and now you feel like nobody. A grandparent or an elder sibling says, "Who you are is far bigger than a title or a team."

Your company closes your team in a restructuring, and you wonder who you are without that job. In the evening, your closest friend calls and says, "Your talent, your values and your kindness did not go anywhere. They are still yours."
helps: Write a short list of who you are beyond one group, one result or one title. Include your values, your strengths and the people who love you.
Ask a parent, an elder or a friend to add to it.
Remind yourself each morning: "I am more than today's result."
Try this today: Add one thing to your list that no result or title can take away.
2.12.read: na tv evaaham jaatu naasam na tvam neme janaadhipaah | na chaiva na bhavishyaamah sarve vayam atah param
2.12.meaning: "There was never a time when I did not exist, or you, or all these people. And none of us will ever cease to be."
2.12.gem: My steady Self (always here, always held)
2.12.bhakti: Krishna says "I, you and all of these," which means every one of us has always been held in His presence. We are never truly alone, even when a group, a title or a place disappears.

stories: You have just moved up from Class 10 to Class 11, and your close friends have been placed in different sections. You scroll through old photos one night and feel a pang. Your elder sibling sits down beside you and says, "Look how much you have grown since those photos, and you are still you. This is just a new chapter."

It is the last week of college, and you are holding your ID card, afraid of what comes next. You do not feel ready to start work. Your parent smiles and says, "You felt exactly the same way on your first day here, and look how it turned out."

You have moved to a new city for your first job and live in a rented room. You miss your old routines and the food at home. A grandparent says on the phone, "This is another stage, like going from childhood to youth. Keep what was good, and welcome what is new."
helps: See change as a stage, not a loss. Think of how much you have already changed since childhood, and notice that you are still you.
Keep one thing from each stage, such as a friend, a habit or a photo.
Welcome one new thing this week, like a new class, a new place or a new person.
Try this today: Send a message to one friend or cousin from an earlier chapter of your life.
2.13.read: dehino 'smin yathaa dehe kaumaaram yauvanam jaraa | tathaa dehaantara- praaptir dheeras tatra na muhyati
2.13.meaning: "Just as the one who lives in this body passes through childhood, youth and old age, in the same way it passes on to another body. A steady person is not troubled by this."
2.13.gem: My steady Self (change is natural, and I stay)
2.13.bhakti: The same "I" has been with you through every stage, and God has been with that "I" all along. He holds the child, the young person and the elder equally.

stories: You post a video of a song you have practised for weeks, and a stranger leaves a mocking comment. It stings all evening, and you keep checking your phone to see if anyone else has said anything. A few days later, your cousin brings it up, and you have to think hard to remember what the comment said.

It is a hot afternoon, and your mother asks you to help clean the house before guests arrive. You would much rather lie down with your phone. The work is tiring and dull, and your first thought is to find a way out of it. But after a few minutes of starting, the discomfort fades, and by evening you feel proud that the house looks bright and your mother looks relaxed.

Your manager sends a sharp email about your report at nine at night. You read it five times, and your stomach tightens. You think about it through dinner. The next morning, he asks, "Can you update the numbers?" as if nothing had happened, and you realise the sting lasted much longer in your mind than in his.
helps: Say, "This will pass." Heat and cold, pleasure and pain all come and go.
Take three slow breaths before you reply to anything that stings.
Do the next small task even while you feel uncomfortable. Many unpleasant things fade once you begin.
Talk it over with a friend, a sibling or a parent if it still hurts after a day or two.
Try this today: Do one small task you have been avoiding, such as a chore at home, for just ten minutes.
2.14.read: maatraa-sparshaas tu kaunteya sheetoshna-sukha-duhkhadaah | aagamaapaayino 'nityaas taams titikshasva bhaarata
2.14.meaning: "The touch of the world on our senses brings cold and heat, pleasure and pain. They come and they go, and none of them lasts. So bear them patiently, Arjuna."
2.14.bhakti: Krishna calls Arjuna "Bharata", a member of a great family, as if to say, "You already have the strength to bear this." When we offer our discomfort to God, it feels lighter.

stories: You top the class test and float through the whole day, posting about it and checking how many people reacted. The next week, a test goes badly, and you feel crushed, as if everything you built has collapsed. Your grandfather says gently, "You are the same person in both weeks."

You play brilliantly in the first match of the college tournament and hear the cheers. In the second match, you drop an easy catch, and your mood sinks so low that you cannot eat dinner. A senior who has played for years tells you, "The best players stay steady after both a cheer and a mistake."

You get a great review at work in March and feel unstoppable. In April you get a difficult one and feel useless. A friend who has been in the job longer says, "Don't let one month decide who you are."
helps: Enjoy the good moments without boasting, and face the hard ones without sinking.
Pause before you share good news online or react to bad news. Ask, "Will this matter next month?"
Learn from a steady person. Watch how a grandparent, a teacher or a senior behaves after both good days and bad days.
Try this today: The next time something good or bad happens, take one slow breath before you react.
2.15.read: yam hi na vyathayanty ete purusham purusharshabha | sama-duhkha- sukham dheeram so 'mritatvaaya kalpate
2.15.meaning: "The steady person, who is not shaken by these feelings and stays the same in pain and in pleasure, becomes ready for lasting freedom."
2.15.bhakti: Evenness is a gift that grows with practice and with grace. A heart that rests in God is like a calm lake, which reflects both sunshine and storm without losing its depth.

stories: You scroll through a classmate's holiday photos, new phone and party pictures, and feel that your own life is dull. Your grandmother says, "A picture is only one moment. Look at what stays: how people treat each other."

In college, your friends begin comparing brands: shoes, phones, watches. You feel the pressure to buy the latest thing, even though your family has to stretch to afford it. A senior who has just started working tells you he wasted money on things he no longer uses, but he still remembers every trip with friends.

At work, a colleague posts about a promotion, a new car and a holiday abroad. You feel a sting of jealousy and wonder if you are falling behind. A friend reminds you that a post is a highlight, not a whole life, and that your steady habits will take you further than quick wins.
helps: Ask, "Is this passing or lasting?" A trend, a look or a number of likes passes. Honesty, learning and kindness last.
Spend your time and money on what lasts: your learning, your health and your friendships.
When jealousy comes, name it, and then wish the other person well. It loosens its grip.
Try this today: Write down one thing you enjoy that no one can see online, and be thankful for it.
2.16.read: naasato vidyate bhaavo naabhaavo vidyate satah | ubhayor api drishto 'ntas tv anayos tattva-darshibhih
2.16.meaning: "What is not lasting has no true existence, and what is truly real never ceases to be. Those who see the truth have understood the nature of both."
2.16.gem: My steady Self (what is passing and what lasts)
2.16.bhakti: Krishna teaches us to look for what truly lasts, and that search leads us to Him.

stories: You forget your lines in the school annual-day play, and a few students laugh. You feel that your confidence has been destroyed. At home, one of your parents says, "Your love for the stage did not leave the building with you. Show me what you will try next."

You lose an election for the college student council after campaigning for weeks. You feel that everything you stood for has been wiped out. An elder you trust says, "The votes are gone, but your ideas and your effort are still yours."
A project you led at work is shelved. You think, "I am no good at this." A senior colleague says, "The project ended. Your skill did not."
helps: List three things about yourself that the failure did not change, such as your kindness, your curiosity or your hard work.
Remember that setbacks happen to what you do, not to who you are.
Ask a parent, a sibling or a close friend to tell you what they still admire in you.
Try this today: Write one sentence that begins, "Even after this, I am still someone who..."
2.17.read: avinaashi tu tad viddhi yena sarvam idam tatam | vinaasham avyayasyaasya na kashchit kartum arhati
2.17.meaning: "Know that to be unbreakable, by which this whole world is filled. No one can destroy that which never changes."
2.17.bhakti: The presence of God within you cannot be taken away by anyone's remark or by any result.

stories: You have been putting off telling your teacher that you do not understand a topic, because you are afraid of how it will sound. Every day you delay, it feels heavier. At last you walk to the staff room, and the teacher smiles and says, "I am glad you came. Let's begin."

You have an assignment due, but each evening something more fun pulls you away, and you tell yourself, "Tomorrow." A friend says, "Start for just fifteen minutes." You open the file, and by the time the fifteen minutes are over, you are already halfway through.

At work, you know you should talk to a colleague about her missed deadlines, but you keep avoiding it, hoping the problem will disappear. Your senior says, "Bring it up kindly and early. Waiting only makes it harder."
helps: Do the first small step today. Fear shrinks once you begin.
Name your duty for this season of life in one line, such as "Finish this assignment by Friday."
Ask a friend or a sibling to check in with you.
Try this today: Set a ten-minute timer and start the task you have been avoiding.
2.18.read: antavanta ime dehaa nityasyoktaah shareerinah | anaashino 'prameyasya tasmaad yudhyasva bhaarata
2.18.meaning: "These bodies come to an end, but the Self that lives in them is eternal, cannot be destroyed and cannot be measured. So, Arjuna, rise and do what must be done."
2.18.gem: Mindful action (do what must be done, without fear)
2.18.bhakti: Krishna gives this instruction with love, as if to say, "Do your part. I am with you." Fear does not get the last word.

stories: In an argument, a friend calls you useless, and you carry that word for days as if it were the truth about you.

You and your group of friends use rough, insulting words for one another as a joke. It seems normal to you. One day a quieter friend stops joining the chat, and you realise the "joke" stung more than you thought.

During a stressful week at work, you snap at a junior colleague and call her work "rubbish." Later she tells you quietly that she was close to tears. You realise that the same Self that was hurt in you earlier lives in her too.
helps: Remember that words describe a moment, not your core. What others say about you does not decide who you are.
Choose your own words with care. Ask, "Would I say this to someone I deeply respect?"
If you hurt someone, say sorry simply, and mean it.
Ask an elder or a friend you trust to tell you honestly how your words sound to others.
Try this today: Replace one rude word you use casually with a kinder one.
2.19.read: ya enam vetti hantaaram yash chainam manyate hatam | ubhau tau na vijaaneeto naayam hanti na hanyate
2.19.meaning: "One who thinks the Self can kill, and one who thinks it can be killed, are both mistaken. The Self neither kills nor is killed."
2.19.bhakti: God lives within every person, untouched, including the one we hurt. Speaking kindly is a way of respecting Him.

stories: Your grandmother, who used to wait for you with warm food after school, has passed away. The house feels very quiet, and you do not know where to put your grief.

A close friend's parent has passed away, and you do not know what to say. You are afraid of saying the wrong thing, so you stay away. Your sibling says, "Just sit with your friend. Being there is enough."

In your first year at work, your grandfather passes away, and you cannot reach home in time. You grieve alone in your rented room. A cousin calls, and you spend an hour sharing stories about him. The grief becomes a little softer.
helps: Allow the grief. Tears are a way of love.
Keep their memory alive with a prayer, a lamp, a favourite story or their favourite food.
Be with family, or call a cousin, an elder or a friend, and share stories.
Sit with a grieving friend even if you have no words.
Try this today: Tell one story about someone you love and miss.
2.20.read: na jaayate mriyate vaa kadaachin naayam bhootvaa bhavitaa vaa na bhooyah | ajo nityah shaashvato 'yam puraano na hanyate hanyamaane shareere
2.20.meaning: "The Self is never born and never dies. It has always been and always will be, ancient and unchanging. It is not destroyed when the body is."
2.20.bhakti: The Gita says that what is truly us is never lost. We can hold those we love in prayer, and their kindness continues to live in us.

parts.title: Part 1: Arjuna's sorrow (2.1–2.10)
parts.intro: Arjuna stands between two armies, overwhelmed by love, duty and fear. These ten verses are about what that feels like and how to begin finding your way.

parts.title: Part 2: Who am I, really? (2.11–2.30)
parts.intro: Krishna's first teaching: you are more than your results, your moods and your roles. Something steady in you does not change with the day.

sk.2.3:
क्लैब्यं मा स्म गमः पार्थ नैतत्त्वय्युपपद्यते ।
क्षुद्रं हृदयदौर्बल्यं त्यक्त्वोत्तिष्ठ परन्तप ॥
sk.2.4:
कथं भीष्ममहं सङ्ख्ये द्रोणं च मधुसूदन ।
इषुभिः प्रतियोत्स्यामि पूजार्हावरिसूदन ॥
sk.2.5:
गुरूनहत्वा हि महानुभावान् श्रेयो भोक्तुं भैक्ष्यमपीह लोके ।
हत्वार्थकामांस्तु गुरूनिहैव भुञ्जीय भोगान् रुधिरप्रदिग्धान् ॥
sk.2.6:
न चैतद्विद्मः कतरन्नो गरीयो यद्वा जयेम यदि वा नो जयेयुः ।
यानेव हत्वा न जिजीविषामस्तेऽवस्थिताः प्रमुखे धार्तराष्ट्राः ॥
sk.2.7:
कार्पण्यदोषोपहतस्वभावः पृच्छामि त्वां धर्मसम्मूढचेताः ।
यच्छ्रेयः स्यान्निश्चितं ब्रूहि तन्मे शिष्यस्तेऽहं शाधि मां त्वां प्रपन्नम् ॥
sk.2.8:
न हि प्रपश्यामि ममापनुद्याद् यच्छोकमुच्छोषणमिन्द्रियाणाम् ।
अवाप्य भूमावसपत्नमृद्धं राज्यं सुराणामपि चाधिपत्यम् ॥
sk.2.9:
एवमुक्त्वा हृषीकेशं गुडाकेशः परन्तप ।
न योत्स्य इति गोविन्दमुक्त्वा तूष्णीं बभूव ह ॥
sk.2.10:
तमुवाच हृषीकेशः प्रहसन्निव भारत ।
सेनयोरुभयोर्मध्ये विषीदन्तमिदं वचः ॥
sk.2.12:
न त्वेवाहं जातु नासं न त्वं नेमे जनाधिपाः ।
न चैव न भविष्यामः सर्वे वयमतः परम् ॥
sk.2.13:
देहिनोऽस्मिन्यथा देहे कौमारं यौवनं जरा ।
तथा देहान्तरप्राप्तिर्धीरस्तत्र न मुह्यति ॥
sk.2.15:
यं हि न व्यथयन्त्येते पुरुषं पुरुषर्षभ ।
समदुःखसुखं धीरं सोऽमृतत्वाय कल्पते ॥
sk.2.16:
नासतो विद्यते भावो नाभावो विद्यते सतः ।
उभयोरपि दृष्टोऽन्तस्त्वनयोस्तत्त्वदर्शिभिः ॥
sk.2.17:
अविनाशि तु तद्विद्धि येन सर्वमिदं ततम् ।
विनाशमव्ययस्यास्य न कश्चित्कर्तुमर्हति ॥
sk.2.18:
अन्तवन्त इमे देहा नित्यस्योक्ताः शरीरिणः ।
अनाशिनोऽप्रमेयस्य तस्माद्युध्यस्व भारत ॥
sk.2.19:
य एनं वेत्ति हन्तारं यश्चैनं मन्यते हतम् ।
उभौ तौ न विजानीतो नायं हन्ति न हन्यते ॥
sk.2.20:
न जायते म्रियते वा कदाचिन्नायं भूत्वा भविता वा न भूयः ।
अजो नित्यः शाश्वतोऽयं पुराणो न हन्यते हन्यमाने शरीरे ॥

ONE.2.1: Krishna lets Arjuna's tears be seen before He says a word. Caring enough to cry is not weakness.
ONE.2.2: Fear and confusion are a fog that has come over you. They are not who you are.
ONE.2.3: Stand up. This heaviness is real, but it is not all of you.
ONE.2.4: Arjuna asks how he can fight the very teachers he respects most.
ONE.2.5: A win that comes from hurting the people who guided you is not worth having.
ONE.2.6: Arjuna admits he does not know what is right, and it is honest to say so.
ONE.2.7: Arjuna stops arguing and asks to be taught. Asking for help is where learning begins.
ONE.2.8: No prize, however big, can fill an ache on the inside.
ONE.2.9: Arjuna runs out of words and goes silent. Silence is not the end of the story.
ONE.2.10: Krishna smiles in the middle of the battlefield. His calm says the storm is not as big as it feels.
ONE.2.11: You already have the wisdom you give to others. Use it on yourself.
ONE.2.12: You have always been you, and you always will be. No group, title or result can change that.
ONE.2.13: Life moves from one stage to the next, and the same "you" goes through all of them.
ONE.2.14: Pleasant and unpleasant feelings both come and go. Bear them patiently, and they pass.
ONE.2.15: Staying the same person on good days and bad days is the way to lasting peace.
ONE.2.16: Much of what feels so important today is only passing. Look for what truly lasts.
ONE.2.17: Something in you cannot be broken by any failure or any remark.
ONE.2.18: Do not let fear make your decisions. Do what must be done with a steady heart.
ONE.2.19: A word cannot harm what you truly are, and the same is true of every other person.
ONE.2.20: What is truly us is never lost, even when someone we love leaves this world.

NEXT.2.4: Your respect for your teachers is good. Krishna will show Arjuna how to keep it and still do his duty.
NEXT.2.5: Krishna will show Arjuna how to act with a clear conscience.
NEXT.2.6: Krishna will show Arjuna the next step, not the whole road.
NEXT.2.7: Krishna begins His teaching only after Arjuna humbly asks. Everything that follows opens from this one step.
NEXT.2.8: Krishna will now turn Arjuna's eyes inward.
NEXT.2.9: Krishna is still right there in the chariot. He does not leave when Arjuna goes silent.

TITLE.2.15: Steady on good days and bad

INDEX: Nerves before an exam, interview or presentation
Friendship trouble and being left out
Choosing a stream, a course or a job
Too much advice, and asking for help
Change, moving and new stages of life
Losing a place, a role or a title
Being there for someone who is upset
gems: My steady Self: something in me stays steady through every change. This is the root of resilience.
Evenness: feelings come and go, and I do not have to be thrown by them.
Mindful action: I give my full attention and best effort, and let go of the result.
Same Self in all: everyone carries the same dignity. This leaves room for kindness, gratitude, sharing and a big heart, and less room for jealousy.
